items.title: fix(cli): validate the loaded agent roster in fast config checks (#20…
items.summary: fix(cli): validate the loaded agent roster in fast config checks (#203520) Root cause: `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.config.ts:99` and `src/cli/update-cli/status.ts:333` validate the config as written with `validateConfigObjectRaw`, skipping `applyImplicitAgentRosterDefaults`, which the normal snapshot load applies first (`src/config/io.snapshot.ts:252`). The schema rule "agents.entries must contain at least one configured agent" is written for the loaded view, so a config without `agents.entries` fails it only in these two readers. Fixes #203505 Thanks @woodmanlegion for the report and the clear trace of the two readers. ## Problem A config with no `agents.entries` is supported since #112678: the normal load adds `{ main: {} }` in memory. `openclaw models set openai/gpt-5` in an empty profile writes exactly that shape. `openclaw config validate` and `openclaw gateway status --deep` say the config is valid, but `openclaw gateway status` (fast path) and `openclaw update status` mark it invalid and send the user to `doctor --fix`, which finds nothing. ## Fix The two fast readers now run the existing `applyImplicitAgentRosterDefaults` before `validateConfigObjectRaw`, the same order the snapshot load uses. No second implementation, no schema change, no config write: the file is unchanged and real config errors still report as before. Callers of the raw validator checked: - `gateway status` fast path (`readFastStatusConfig`): had the gap, fixed. - `update status` (`readSourceConfigBestEffort` + raw check): had the gap, fixed. Other callers of `readSourceConfigBestEffort` do not validate. - Doctor repair, heartbeat repair, setup native runtime: validate `snapshot.sourceConfig` or a loaded config, already normalized. ## Evidence Built CLI in a secretless `node:24.22.1` container, empty profile per scenario, `openclaw models set openai/gpt-5`, then the four commands. Full output: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203520#issuecomment-7081137938 | Scenario | Build | gateway status | update status | config validate | gateway status --deep | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | defaults only (no `entries`) | main | invalid | invalid | valid | valid | | defaults only (no `entries`) | this PR | valid | valid | valid | valid | | explicit `entries.main` | main / this PR | valid | valid | valid | valid | | `ownership: "explicit"`, no entries | main / this PR | invalid (same message) | invalid | invalid | invalid | | `gateway.port: "not-a-port"` | this PR | invalid (port issue only) | invalid | invalid | invalid | On main the port scenario also lists the false `agents.entries` line next to the port issue in the two fast commands; this PR drops only that line. The config file hash is unchanged after every run. Tests: two existing fast-read cases (`status.gather` fast config read, `update status` remote JSON) now carry a defaults-only `agents` section; both fail on main and pass here. Size: production +4/-2, tests +3/-0 against the merge base; no new helper, flag or state. ## Merge danger Two-way door: read-only diagnostics, no state or config written; a revert fully restores the old output. Blast radius: the config-validity lines of `openclaw gateway status` (fast path) and `openclaw update status`. Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi

items.title: refactor: drop tool-caller re-checks from Gateway-side callers (#203503)
items.summary: refactor: drop tool-caller re-checks from Gateway-side callers (#203503) ## What Problem This Solves #203487 made `captureGatewayToolCallerAssertion` stop re-checking permission in the middle of a started tool call. Its Gateway-side callers still captured it and called it again at every step. That is dead weight: after #203487 the call only checks Stop, and most of these callers already check Stop through their own request signal or commit guard. ## Why This Change Was Made Admission checks permission one time, when work starts. This PR removes the leftover capture from the Gateway-side callers, so the per-step re-check path is gone there. Removed (capture and its calls): - `server-methods/themes.ts`, `tools-github.ts`, `users-personal-file.ts`, `environments.session.ts`, `request-authorization.ts` (startup exemption for admitted runs); - `session-access-authority.ts`, `session-runtime-authority.ts`; - `server-plugin-in-process-dispatch.ts` (`runWithInProcessGatewaySessionMutation`); - `server-plugin-in-process-authority.ts` (continuation capture); - `github-publication-auto-fix.ts`; - `plugins/service-session-work.ts`. Where a caller used "capture returned a function" only to mean "this is an admitted agent run", it now reads `caller.operationalRunInstance`, which is the same condition the capture tested. `resolveSessionRuntimeAuthority` now returns nothing when no runtime identity exists (the caller-only branch was a Stop check only). Stop still applies at every changed site: - In-process Gateway methods (themes, GitHub read, personal file, environments, auto-fix, session mutation) still call `sessionMutationCommitGuard` / `resolved.assertContextCurrent`, which keeps the caller's Stop and receipt fence (see below). - `tools-github` and `environments.session` already combine `caller.approvalSignals` into their signal. - Service session work keeps Stop through `captureAmbientGatewayOperatorAuthority().assertInvocationCurrent`. - The continuation capture now checks `caller.approvalSignals` directly at the same point. Kept on purpose (cut less): two sites carry the capture's receipt fence into session commit guards, so they keep it until PR 6 removes the lease at `captureAdmittedRunActiveAssertion`: - `resolveInProcessGatewayDispatch().assertContextCurrent` (`server-plugin-in-process-authority.ts`); - `captureOperatorToolGatewayAuthority` / `captureAmbientGatewayOperatorAuthority` (`operator-invocation-authority.ts`, left unchanged). The receipt fences the writing run (lease held, same run instance), which the session owner's `sessionMutationAuthorization` does not cover; an abort signal cannot replace it. No new export, name, hook, flag or guard. ## User Impact None visible. A tool call that was admitted keeps running to the end; Stop still cancels it; writes to a replaced or locked session still fail with the session conflict. Gateway methods during startup still accept admitted agent runs. ## Evidence - Pre-push: one `ocx test` run with fail-fast off over 113 files (the touched sources' own tests, every direct importer of a changed file, importers of the 12 touched `*.test-support.ts` dependencies, and every test that names `captureGatewayToolCallerAssertion`): 112 files green. `server.private-completion.test.ts` timed out one case under host load (22.9 s wait) and cascaded into its sibling case; alone it passes 27/27. - `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test`, oxfmt and oxlint on the changed files: clean. - No test asserted a refusal through these callers, so no test was deleted. - Production: 11 files, +43 / −91. `config/session-identity-allowlist.txt`: `request-authorization.ts` 7 → 6 (the removed refusal string was a counted pin). - Real Gateway E2E (one-admission journey) on the final head `f3c8465e7234`: Q (revoke while queued → refused visibly), R (revoke while running → finishes), S (Stop → cancels) all pass: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203503#issuecomment-7080659777 - Local review on the final head: patch correct, zero findings. - CI: every red job is MAIN-ALSO, with per-test base evidence in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203503#issuecomment-7081466082 (#203512, #203527). Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi

items.title: refactor: drop tool-caller re-checks from session tools and subagent …
items.summary: refactor: drop tool-caller re-checks from session tools and subagent registry (#203516) ## What Problem This Solves #203487 made `captureGatewayToolCallerAssertion` stop re-checking permission in the middle of a started tool call; it now only checks Stop and carries the caller receipt's session fences. The `sessions_*` tools and the subagent registry still captured it and called it again at each step. Those calls are dead weight. Some of them also used "the capture returned a function" to mean "this is an admitted agent run". ## Why This Change Was Made Admission checks permission one time, when work starts. This PR removes the leftover capture from the session tools and the subagent registry: - `sessions-list-tool.ts`: the capture and its call in `finalize`; the tool signal check stays. - `sessions-tool.ts` (`assign_owner`), `sessions-tool-control.ts` (`captureSessionStopCaller`, `stopSessionTool`): the admitted-run gate reads `caller.operationalRunInstance`, which is the condition the capture tested. The tool signal check stays at each step. - `sessions-operator-authority.ts`: the `sessions.patch` capture is removed from the composed control source. - `sessions-send-communication.ts`: the capture is removed from `assertSource`, which already checks the tool call's `signal` and closes on abort. The approval gate reads `caller.operationalRunInstance`. - `sessions-send-tool.delivery.ts`, `sessions-send-tool.steering.ts`: the steering guard still uses the guarded (V2) injection for an admitted run. Stop reaches it through `assertSendCurrent` (the communication assertion, which is signal-bound). - `sessions-send-followup.ts`, `sessions-send-followup-custody.ts`: the follow-up checks are the prepared custody (`request.custody.assertCurrent`) only. - `sessions-send-resume.ts`, `gateway/session-subagent-resume.ts`: a live admitted caller has no `assertCurrent`. A host-retained replay keeps its retained source assertion. `requirePausedChild` runs `caller.assertCurrent?.()`; admission is decided once in `captureSessionsSendResumeCaller` (the only producer of this caller). - `subagent-registry-public-api.ts`, `subagent-registry-requester-claim.ts`: the registry writes keep the state-worker source check and the continuation custody. Session write fences are not dropped. Every sessions tool write goes through the in-process Gateway caller (`in-process-gateway.ts`, PR 1d), which still composes the caller's receipt into `sessionMutationCommitGuard`. The removed captures were all sync closures (Stop only) or duplicated that composed fence. No new export, name, hook, flag or guard. Production: 13 files, +43 / −108. Accepted edge cases (no code for them): - `acknowledgeSubagentResultForRequesterTurn` and `claimSubagentYield` no longer check Stop before their registry write. These are internal bookkeeping writes for a result the run already has (mark delivered, record the yield), not user-visible effects. - `prepareSessionsSendFollowup` no longer checks the tool Stop during its preparation reads. The dispatch that follows stays signal-fenced through the communication assertion. ### Changed tests - `sessions-tool.self-archive.test.ts`, `agent-tools.session-owner.test.ts`: `sessions.assignOwner` no longer carries `assertDispatchCurrent`. - `sessions-send-communication.test.ts`: the mocked caller now has an `operationalRunInstance` (that is what "admitted" means now); the removed capture mock is gone. No test asserted a mid-run refusal through these callers, so no test was deleted. ## User Impact None visible. An admitted session tool call runs to the end; Stop still cancels it; writes to a replaced or locked session still fail with the session conflict. ## Evidence - Pre-push: one `ocx test` run with fail-fast off over 41 files (every direct importer of a changed source, plus importers of the test-support files that import them). After the test fixes, everything is green except: - `agent.test.ts` ("honors owner cancellation while explicit recipient session routing is pending", "does not deliver prepared identity after the client loses authority") and `question.communication.test.ts` ("retains creator/admin rights without treating assigned responsibility as authority"): also red on the merge base `6ff7a062e54e`. - `server.plugin-reload-send-revocation.product.test.ts`: it expects "Operator access was revoked; start a new user turn.", which no production code emits since #202513. On head the revoked replay is still refused with 0 effects; the notice says "Restart recovery operator authority changed; start a new user turn.". On the base it timed out under host load. - `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test`, oxfmt and oxlint on the changed files: clean. - Head E2E: Q, R and S pass (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203516#issuecomment-7081096588). Local review on the final head: patch correct, zero findings. Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi
